stories.headline: Manhunt underway after a shooting at a California Spirit Halloween store leaves 1 dead and 6 hurt
stories.summary: Police in Fairfield, California, are hunting for a gunman who opened fire inside a Spirit Halloween store at the Solano Town Center mall around 8:30 p.m. Friday, killing one person and wounding six. Police Chief Dan Marshall said at least three of the injured are in critical condition, and detectives are still working to identify the suspect or suspects. One shopper's husband told NBC affiliate KCRA that his wife heard "five big bangs" and escaped with others through an emergency exit on the far side of the mall. Hours earlier, a 21-year-old Detroit man was seriously wounded in a shooting inside a Spirit Halloween store in Madison Heights, Michigan, where bystanders tackled the 21-year-old suspect before police took him into custody.

stories.headline: Apple sends stores a memo on the iPhone Duo's inner-screen cracks and tells techs to repair or replace affected phones
stories.summary: Apple has sent Apple Stores and authorized service providers an internal memo on how to diagnose and handle the iPhone Duo's inner display cracking problem, MacRumors reports. If a customer reports a crack, technicians are told to inspect the phone and repair or replace it under standard procedures. The memo repeats Apple's public line that only "a small number" of units are affected and that defective units tend to show the problem soon after use. There is no recall and no public repair program yet, but the fact that Apple issued guidance suggests the issue is common enough to need it. Owners who see a crack can contact AppleCare online or at 1-800-APL-CARE.

stories.headline: DOJ calls the 'second Dan Sullivan' allegations troubling and asks a judge to set aside Alaska ballots that rank him
stories.summary: Alaska's U.S. attorney, Michael Heyman, said Friday that reports Democratic operatives helped recruit Daniel J. Sullivan, who shares a name with GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan, as a sham Senate candidate are "troubling" and have brought "a significant surge of law enforcement assets" to the state, though he would not say what crimes are being investigated. In a separate civil case, the Justice Department asked for an injunction to preserve and segregate every ballot that ranks Daniel J. Sullivan, plus fast-track discovery from Mary Peltola's campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, with a ruling requested by Monday. Peltola and national Democrats deny any role. Alaska opposes the request, saying ballots are mixed on Election Day, can't be separated without breaking ballot secrecy, and are already kept for 22 months.

stories.headline: Trumbull traffic stop that turned up 21 kilos of hidden cocaine ends with 10-year federal sentences for two men
stories.summary: Two Connecticut men caught with about 21 kilograms of cocaine during a state police traffic stop in Trumbull have each been sentenced to 10 years in federal prison, followed by five years of supervised release, federal prosecutors said. Troopers stopped their 2024 Subaru Crosstrek in Trumbull on Feb. 23 as part of a federal investigation, and after a K-9 alerted, they found the drugs in two hidden compartments built in under the front seats. Driver Reginald Rogers, 38, of Woodbridge and passenger Lester Arrington, 34, of Naugatuck pleaded guilty to possessing five kilograms or more of cocaine with intent to distribute and forfeited the car. They were sentenced this week in Bridgeport and must report to prison on Jan. 13.

stories.headline: Jets-Raiders preview: 2-5 New York says it must finish close games when Las Vegas visits Sunday at 1 p.m.
stories.summary: The Jets (2-5) host the Las Vegas Raiders (3-4) at MetLife Stadium on Sunday at 1 p.m., and the theme of the week is finishing. New York has lost four one-possession games, including last week's 28-25 loss to the previously winless Dolphins, while the Raiders have dropped four straight after a 3-0 start. Coach Aaron Glenn said everyone, "from coaching to playing," has to be better and that "our fans deserve better than that, and that starts with me." Geno Smith said the team believes in its direction but has to close out games, and Garrett Wilson, who has said he wants to stay a Jet, pointed to execution "at the biggest moment." The offense has scored on its last three opening drives; the defense has worked all week on starting faster.

stories.headline: Four NASA volunteers walk out of a simulated Mars habitat in Houston this weekend after nearly 380 days inside
stories.summary: Four volunteers who have lived for almost 380 days inside a Mars habitat simulator at NASA's Johnson Space Center are due to emerge on Saturday, ending the second CHAPEA mission. The crew spent more than a year without sunlight, shopping or in-person contact with family, while NASA studied how isolation, distance and a harsh environment affect people before it sends astronauts into deep space. Inside the hangar they ran simulated spacewalks, performed experiments and tested technology, and learned to cut their own hair, fix the plumbing and even draw their own blood. One crew member called it "extreme camping." Because of the simulation's conditions, the crew couldn't give live interviews; NASA shared a podcast in which they described the year.

stories.headline: SpaceX reportedly wants access to 80,000 cell sites to turn Starlink into a carrier that rivals Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile
stories.summary: Elon Musk's SpaceX is reportedly negotiating for access to at least 80,000 cell sites across the U.S. as it explores turning Starlink into a full nationwide wireless carrier. Tower owner Crown Castle, which runs about 40,000 towers, told investors on Oct. 21 that "you can assume that we're talking to all parties." The idea is to pair satellites, which cover remote areas but struggle to reach phones indoors, with ground towers for stronger everyday service, and SpaceX has also discussed putting small base stations in Starlink customers' home equipment. Earlier this month Grain Management agreed to sell SpaceX its nationwide 800 MHz spectrum, a deal that still needs FCC approval. The talks are preliminary, and SpaceX hasn't confirmed any tower agreements.

stories.headline: Dee Snider and Headbangers Ball host Riki Rachtman team up for a new metal video podcast, 'The Ball'
stories.summary: Twisted Sister's Dee Snider and Riki Rachtman, the former Cathouse club owner who hosted MTV's "Headbangers Ball" from 1990, have launched a new metal podcast called "The Ball," and the first episode is now up on YouTube. The pairing nods to MTV history: Snider hosted the debut of "Heavy Metal Mania" in 1985, the show that was later replaced by "Headbangers Ball" in 1987. Rachtman said the new show will be on YouTube, Spotify and iTunes but is also filmed as a video program on a set that "looks insane." A Patreon will let fans take part live, because the show will be recorded in front of them.

stories.headline: Staples High girls basketball coach resigns after police say he tripped and choked a referee at a youth game
stories.summary: Thomas Sparks, 37, the girls basketball coach at Westport's Staples High School, has resigned after he was arrested on charges that he tripped and choked a referee over a foul call during a Connecticut Elite youth league game in Shelton on Oct. 24. According to the police report cited by the CT Post, Sparks argued with the referee and then wrapped his arm around his neck before people in the crowd pulled him off; witnesses, including some players, backed the referee's account. He was charged with assault, strangulation and risk of injury to a child and released on $10,000 bond. Staples' athletic director said he resigned Thursday for "personal and family considerations," and he no longer works for Connecticut Elite. He is due back in court Nov. 12.

stories.headline: 'Looks like Mars': Indonesia's worst fire season in a decade is choking Southeast Asia in toxic smog
stories.summary: Months of wildfires in Indonesia have smothered parts of Southeast Asia in yellow-orange smoke, closing schools in several countries and driving a spike in breathing problems. Indonesia's forests and peatlands burn every year as farms clear land by slash-and-burn, but heat and drought from a "super" El Niño have made this the worst season in more than a decade. "It looks like Mars, like we're living on another planet," said Natanael Undas, a teacher in Central Kalimantan who has tracked the haze since 2014 and whose 2-year-old daughter sneezes constantly even with the windows shut. Hundreds of students and activists protested in Jakarta and other cities this week, accusing the government of doing too little, while neighboring countries are threatening prosecutions.

stories.headline: Penguins visit red-hot Montreal tonight after Thursday's last-second collapse against Utah
stories.summary: The Penguins play at Montreal on Saturday night, two days after a gut-punch 4-3 overtime loss to Utah in which Pittsburgh led with 25 seconds left, only for Pittsburgh native Logan Cooley to complete a hat trick with one second remaining before Mikhail Sergachev won it in OT. "We need to play, like, so much harder, whole five guys," said Evgeni Malkin, who had two assists; Kris Letang said "the performance was not there," though goalie Arturs Silovs made 30 saves. Teenager Ben Kindel scored in his return after a medical scare on the team plane. The Canadiens come home on a four-game win streak, with Cole Caufield leading the team with eight goals and Lane Hutson setting a franchise record for assists by a player under 23.

stories.headline: LEGO and Nike launch a Classic Space basketball collection, with sneakers that nod to Ice Planet 2002
stories.summary: LEGO and Nike are rolling out a kids' basketball collection built around LEGO's retro Classic Space theme. It is led by the Nike Air Force 1 Low LV8, styled like an astronaut's spacesuit with sketched stitching, a Classic Space-inspired Swoosh and a nod to LEGO's Ice Planet 2002 line, plus the Nike S.T. Dynamite with a color-shifting finish and glitter sole. A backpack, shorts, T-shirt, hoodie and cargo pants carry the Classic Space logo. The range launches Nov. 2 in the U.K. and parts of Europe, and the full lineup reaches North America on Nov. 24.

stories.headline: Russian drone strikes on power plants and substations leave nearly 300,000 Ukrainian households in the dark
stories.summary: Russian attacks on Ukraine's energy grid overnight left around 200,000 households in Dnipro and the surrounding Dnipropetrovsk region and more than 80,000 in the Kyiv region without electricity, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Saturday. Shahed drones hit a combined heat and power plant in Kyiv on Friday evening; overnight, Russian forces struck four electrical substations in Dnipropetrovsk, a power plant in Shostka in the Sumy region, a gas facility, and rail infrastructure in Dnipro and Kharkiv. Russia launched 134 drones in all, with hits recorded at 20 locations. Repair crews are working to restore power as winter approaches.

stories.headline: Big Oil books another quarter of huge profits as the Iran war keeps crude above $110 and gas $1.20 higher than a year ago
stories.summary: ExxonMobil, Chevron and Shell together earned just over $36 billion this quarter, with Exxon more than doubling its profit from a year ago to $15.4 billion, as the war in Iran keeps oil from the Middle East off the market. Brent crude is around $113 a barrel, up from about $70 before the war, and AAA says gasoline costs about $1.20 a gallon more than a year ago; diesel hit a record in September. Most of the windfall is going to shareholders through record dividends and buybacks rather than new drilling, because executives see the high prices as driven by geopolitics. Shell's CEO said low global inventories mean prices could stay high for some time. Democrats are again pushing a windfall-profits tax, which Exxon calls "misguided."

stories.headline: Apple Intelligence finally comes to China in iOS 27.3, with a beta on Nov. 4 and a full release in December
stories.summary: Apple says Apple Intelligence is launching in China with iOS 27.3, starting with a beta on Nov. 4 and a public release planned for December. The first features are the older ones: notification summaries, live translation, writing and proofreading tools, Visual Intelligence and removing objects from photos. The new AI-powered Siri isn't part of it. Apple also worked with Alibaba to bring its Qwen chatbot into some features, much like the ChatGPT integration in the U.S. Chinese regulators approved Apple Intelligence in July, and Reuters reported that Apple trained its own large language model specifically for China.

stories.headline: Lamb of God's Headbangers Boat metal cruise will sail from England for the first time in 2028
stories.summary: Lamb of God's metal cruise, Headbangers Boat, will sail from Southampton, England, to La Coruña, Spain, on May 27–31, 2028, the first time it has left from British shores. It is the fifth edition of the cruise, aboard the Norwegian Jewel. Paleface Swiss, Bleed From Within, Heriot, Shadows Fall and Kublai Khan TX are booked so far, with more acts to come. The band will host extras: frontman Randy Blythe will do an in-depth Q&A, drummer Art Cruz will spin a DJ set, and bassist John Campbell will sit at the final table of a poker tournament. There will also be metal trivia and karaoke.

stories.headline: Gizmodo's best gadgets of October 2026, from Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro to a speaker shaped like a milk carton
stories.summary: Gizmodo's consumer tech team has rounded up the best gadgets of a packed "Techtober." Apple spent the back half of the month launching hardware: the HomeView smart home display and a set of smart home devices made with LG, M6 iMacs and MacBook Pros, and, at long last, an OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro with M5 Pro and Max chips. Other companies followed with new audio, photography and smart home gear. Picks include the first wireless speaker from Nothing spin-off CMF, which looks like a milk carton, sounds good, pairs in stereo and has 3D-printable face plates and buttons. The list is a handy catch-up on what launched before the holiday shopping season.

stories.headline: Overnight repaving on Route 111 (Main Street) in Trumbull will start after the polls close on Election Day
stories.summary: The Connecticut Department of Transportation will mill and resurface a short stretch of Route 111 (Main Street) in Trumbull between Whalburn Avenue and Chestnut Hill Road, the town said Friday. To avoid traffic trouble on Election Day, crews from Waters Construction won't start until the polls close on Tuesday, Nov. 3, and will work overnight to finish on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Drivers should expect lane closures on that 0.09-mile segment, with traffic control personnel, signs and local police guiding motorists through the work zone. CTDOT says the schedule could change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions and asks drivers to keep their speed down in the area.

stories.headline: Clocks fall back this Sunday: daylight saving time ends at 2 a.m. on Nov. 1
stories.summary: Daylight saving time ends for 2026 this weekend, so most of the U.S. sets clocks back one hour at 2 a.m. on Sunday, Nov. 1, and everyone gets an extra hour of sleep. Mornings get lighter and evenings darker: in Boston, for example, sunrise moves from 7:16 a.m. on Saturday to 6:17 a.m. on Sunday, and sunset from 5:39 p.m. to 4:37 p.m. The U.S. first adopted the clock change in 1918 during World War I to save fuel, and Congress didn't set uniform start and end dates until 1966. This year, the Sunshine Protection Act, which would make daylight saving time permanent and let states opt out, passed the House in July and now sits in the Senate, where President Trump has accused Arkansas Sen. Tom Cotton of holding it up.

stories.headline: Trumbull this week: early voting’s final week at the library, a Town Hall Halloween parade for preschoolers, and a Hillcrest update
stories.summary: Early voting runs its final week in the Trumbull Library Community Room, 33 Quality St., from Monday, Oct. 26, through Sunday, Nov. 1. Hours are 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., extended to 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Tuesday and Thursday. Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, with polls open 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. On Tuesday, Oct. 27, at 10 and 11:30 a.m., Town Hall staff host a costume parade and trick-or-treating past decorated office doors for registered Trumbull kids ages 0 to 5. Each session is limited to 20 children. That evening the Hillcrest Middle School Building Committee gets project updates and the EMS Commission reviews vehicles, staffing and plans for Trumbull EMS’s 50th anniversary. The Conservation Commission meets Wednesday on tree rules and a spring 2027 tree giveaway.
